llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions largely match its stated SeaArt video-generation purpose, but there are small metadata inconsistencies and token-handling details you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill name, description, SKILL.md, README, and the included Python script all consistently implement SeaArt text-to-video and image-to-video generation and require only a SeaArt session token. However the registry metadata claims no required binaries while SKILL.md lists 'python3' as required and the script requires the 'requests' library — the declared requirements are inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stay within the stated purpose: they ask for a SeaArt session cookie (T) saved as SEAART_TOKEN, check that env var, and run the bundled Python script which calls only seaart.ai endpoints. The instructions do direct the user to persist the token with `/update-config`, which stores the token in the local agent config — this is expected for convenience but increases the blast radius if that config is accessible to others.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads are present (instruction-only plus an included script). The risk surface is limited to the provided script; there are no external install URLs or archive extractions. You should still install the 'requests' Python dependency manually or verify it's available.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one secret (SEAART_TOKEN) is required, which is proportional to the stated functionality. Minor inconsistency: registry metadata lists no primaryEnv while SKILL.md and the script require SEAART_TOKEN as the auth token — the registry should declare SEAART_TOKEN as the primary credential. No other unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges. The only persistence action described is storing the SEAART_TOKEN in the user's agent config via `/update-config`, which is a normal convenience but should be considered sensitive storage.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (call seaart.ai using your session cookie). Before installing: 1) Confirm you have Python 3 and the 'requests' library available (the script requires them). 2) Be aware the skill asks you to extract your 'T' cookie from the browser and persist it as SEAART_TOKEN; treat that value like a password and ensure your agent config file is private. 3) The registry metadata omits required binaries/primary credential — verify your environment will provide python3 and that SEAART_TOKEN will be stored securely. 4) Inspect scripts/generate.py yourself (it's included) and consider running the script locally once with test inputs to confirm behavior. 5) Do not paste your token into chat or share it; only set it via your agent's secure config mechanism. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for corrected metadata (declare python3 and SEAART_TOKEN as primary) or run the script in an isolated environment.
